curve/def: The sigmoid squashes any number into the range zero to one. Written sigma of x, with the Greek letter sigma, it is one over one plus e to the minus x.
curve/zero: At zero, e to the zero is one, so sigma is one over two: a half.
curve/two: At two, e to the minus two is about zero point one four. One over one point one four is about zero point eight eight.
curve/tails: Far to the right it creeps up toward one, and far to the left down toward zero.
curve/neg: At minus two, minus x is two, so e to the minus x is e squared: about seven point three nine. One over eight point three nine is about zero point one two: below a half, as every negative input gives.
measure/nudge: How steep is the sigmoid? Measure it as for any curve. Nudge x from zero to zero point zero one, and sigma goes from a half to zero point five zero two five.
measure/measure: It rose zero point zero zero two five over a run of zero point zero one: a slope of a quarter. And a quarter is a half times a half, which is sigma times one minus sigma.
measure/two: At two, the same nudge raises sigma by about zero point zero zero one zero five. Over the run of zero point zero one, that is a slope of about zero point one zero five.
measure/match: Sigma there is about zero point eight eight one, and one minus it is zero point one one nine. Their product is about zero point one zero five: the same again.
measure/rule: That holds at every x: the slope, d sigma, d x, is sigma times one minus sigma. Backprop can build it from the output it already has.
slope/plot: Plot that slope at every x. It peaks at zero, where sigma is a half, at a quarter, and falls away on both sides.
slope/chain: In a graph, the sigmoid node multiplies the gradient from above, partial f, partial sigma, by this local slope. Say two arrives, at x equals two. Then x gets two times zero point one zero five: about zero point two one.
slope/most: Wherever x is, the slope is at most a quarter. So x gets at most a quarter of what arrives: with two from above, never more than a half.
flat/six: Far from zero the curve goes flat. At six, sigma is zero point nine nine seven five.
flat/tiny: So its slope is zero point nine nine seven five times zero point zero zero two five: about zero point zero zero two five.
flat/mirror: At minus six, it is the mirror image: sigma is zero point zero zero two five, one minus sigma is zero point nine nine seven five, and the slope is the same.
flat/dead: Almost no gradient gets through. A saturated sigmoid, stuck near zero or one, passes almost nothing back to the nodes before it.
